import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def quick_select_precond (v : Array Int) (k : Nat) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  k < v.size
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- A canonical sorted version of a list, used as the specification witness. -/
def sortI (l : List Int) : List Int := List.insertionSort (· ≤ ·) l

/-- Quick select on lists: partition around the head pivot and recurse. -/
def qsel (l : List Int) (k : Nat) : Int :=
  match l with
  | [] => 0
  | p :: rest =>
    if k < (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))).length then
      qsel (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))) k
    else if k = (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))).length then
      p
    else
      qsel (rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)))
        (k - (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))).length - 1)
termination_by l.length
decreasing_by
  all_goals simp only [List.length_cons, List.length_unattach]
  all_goals refine Nat.lt_succ_of_le (le_trans (List.length_filter_le _ _) ?_)
  all_goals simp
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def quick_select (v : Array Int) (k : Nat) (h_precond : quick_select_precond v k) : Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  qsel v.toList k
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def quick_select_postcond (v : Array Int) (k : Nat) (result : Int) (h_precond : quick_select_precond v k) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  ∃ sorted : List Int,
    sorted.length = v.size ∧
    List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) sorted ∧
    sorted.getD k 0 = result ∧
    sorted.Perm v.toList
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem sortI_perm (l : List Int) : (sortI l).Perm l :=
  List.perm_insertionSort _ _

theorem sortI_sorted (l : List Int) : List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) (sortI l) :=
  List.sorted_insertionSort _ _

theorem sortI_length (l : List Int) : (sortI l).length = l.length :=
  (sortI_perm l).length_eq

theorem mem_sortI_lo {p x : Int} {rest : List Int}
    (h : x ∈ sortI (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)))) : x < p := by
  have h' := (sortI_perm _).mem_iff.mp h
  rw [List.mem_filter] at h'
  exact of_decide_eq_true h'.2

theorem mem_sortI_hi {p y : Int} {rest : List Int}
    (h : y ∈ sortI (rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)))) : p ≤ y := by
  have h' := (sortI_perm _).mem_iff.mp h
  rw [List.mem_filter] at h'
  have h2 := h'.2
  simp only [Bool.not_eq_true', decide_eq_false_iff_not, not_lt] at h2
  exact h2

theorem sortI_cons (p : Int) (rest : List Int) :
    sortI (p :: rest) =
      sortI (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))) ++
        p :: sortI (rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p))) := by
  refine List.eq_of_perm_of_sorted ?_ (sortI_sorted _) ?_
  · have e1 : (sortI (p :: rest)).Perm (p :: rest) := sortI_perm _
    have e2 : (p :: rest).Perm (p :: (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)) ++
        rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)))) :=
      List.Perm.cons p (List.filter_append_perm (fun x => decide (x < p)) rest).symm
    have e3 : (p :: (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)) ++
        rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)))).Perm
        (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)) ++
          p :: rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p))) := List.perm_middle.symm
    have e4 : (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)) ++
        p :: rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p))).Perm
        (sortI (rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p))) ++
          p :: sortI (rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)))) :=
      List.Perm.append (sortI_perm _).symm (List.Perm.cons p (sortI_perm _).symm)
    exact ((e1.trans e2).trans e3).trans e4
  · refine List.pairwise_append.mpr ⟨sortI_sorted _, ?_, ?_⟩
    · refine List.pairwise_cons.mpr ⟨fun b hb => mem_sortI_hi hb, sortI_sorted _⟩
    · intro x hx y hy
      rcases List.mem_cons.mp hy with hy | hy
      · exact le_of_lt (hy ▸ mem_sortI_lo hx)
      · exact le_of_lt (lt_of_lt_of_le (mem_sortI_lo hx) (mem_sortI_hi hy))

theorem qsel_eq : ∀ (n : Nat) (l : List Int) (k : Nat), l.length ≤ n → k < l.length →
    qsel l k = (sortI l).getD k 0 := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => intro l k h1 h2; omega
  | succ n ih =>
    intro l k h1 h2
    cases l with
    | nil => simp at h2
    | cons p rest =>
      rw [qsel, sortI_cons p rest]
      set lo := rest.filter (fun x => decide (x < p)) with hlodef
      set hi := rest.filter (fun x => !decide (x < p)) with hhidef
      have hlen : lo.length + hi.length = rest.length := by
        have h := (List.filter_append_perm (fun x => decide (x < p)) rest).length_eq
        rw [List.length_append] at h
        exact h
      have hslo : (sortI lo).length = lo.length := sortI_length _
      have hshi : (sortI hi).length = hi.length := sortI_length _
      have hrest : k < rest.length + 1 := by simpa using h2
      have hn : rest.length ≤ n := by simpa using h1
      split_ifs with hc1 hc2
      · rw [ih lo k (by omega) hc1]
        rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
          List.getElem?_append_left (by omega)]
      · rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
          List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)]
        have : k - (sortI lo).length = 0 := by omega
        rw [this]
        simp
      · rw [ih hi (k - lo.length - 1) (by omega) (by omega)]
        rw [List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD, List.getD_eq_getElem?_getD,
          List.getElem?_append_right (by omega)]
        have : k - (sortI lo).length = (k - lo.length - 1) + 1 := by omega
        rw [this, List.getElem?_cons_succ]
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem quick_select_postcond_satisfied (v : Array Int) (k : Nat) (h_precond : quick_select_precond v k) :
    quick_select_postcond v k (quick_select v k h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  refine ⟨sortI v.toList, ?_, sortI_sorted _, ?_, sortI_perm _⟩
  · rw [sortI_length]; simp
  · exact (qsel_eq v.toList.length v.toList k le_rfl (by simpa using h_precond)).symm
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What I did

**Implementation** (`code` section): `quick_select v k _ = qsel v.toList k`, where `qsel` (in `auxcode`) is a genuine recursive partition-based quick select:

```lean
def qsel (l : List Int) (k : Nat) : Int :=
  match l with
  | [] => 0
  | p :: rest =>
    if k < lo.length then qsel lo k
    else if k = lo.length then p
    else qsel hi (k - lo.length - 1)
```

with `lo = rest.filter (· < p)`, `hi = rest.filter (¬ · < p)`. Termination is by `l.length`; the `decreasing_by` goals need `List.length_unattach` because Lean's WF preprocessing rewrites `filter` over `attach`.

**Proof strategy** (`lemma`/`proof` sections):
- `sortI l := List.insertionSort (· ≤ ·) l` is the canonical sorted witness, with `sortI_perm`, `sortI_sorted`, `sortI_length`.
- `sortI_cons`: `sortI (p :: rest) = sortI lo ++ p :: sortI hi`. Proved by uniqueness of sorted permutations (`List.eq_of_perm_of_sorted`): the RHS is a permutation of `p :: rest` (via `List.filter_append_perm` and `List.perm_middle`) and is sorted (`List.pairwise_append` plus the facts that every element of `lo` is `< p` and every element of `hi` is `≥ p`).
- `qsel_eq`: by induction on a length bound, `qsel l k = (sortI l).getD k 0` for `k < l.length`. The three branches of `qsel` line up with indexing into `sortI lo ++ p :: sortI hi` on the left part, at the pivot, and on the right part, using `List.getElem?_append_left/right`.
- The postcondition then follows with `sortI v.toList` as the existential witness.
